intro: Above you rises Ankara Castle, a castle and walls in Ankara province from the 7th century AD. This citadel wraps the hill the city grew on. Look closely at its walls: they were built course by course from column drums and inscribed blocks stripped out of Roman buildings.
history: The present walls went up in the seventh century, when Byzantium was building a defensive line against Arab raids. The builders took what lay at hand. Most of the material was stripped from the city's Roman buildings, so column drums, funerary stelae and inscribed blocks now stand side by side in the masonry. Under the Seljuks and Ottomans the castle was repaired and kept in use.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the inner citadel, the eastern tower, the walls of reused stone and the Alâeddin Mosque.
facts: Did you know? The inscribed blocks in these walls are the largest single collection of Ankara's Roman gravestones, and not one of them is in a museum. They are all here, in the wall. The present walls were built in the seventh century, when Byzantium was raising a defensive line against Arab raids.
outro: This brings our tour of Ankara Castle to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
